overview:
Two thousand years of Moroccan history in one easy day from Fez: the Roman city of Volubilis in the cool of the morning, a view over the holy town of Moulay Idriss, and then a real afternoon in Meknes, the imperial capital of Sultan Moulay Ismail. Most day trips give Meknes about an hour at the end of the day. This one gives it around four, so you can walk under the great gate of Bab Mansour, stand inside the vast granaries of Heri es-Souani and wander a medina that is calmer and friendlier than the one in Fez.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours, door to door
• Start and finish: your riad or hotel in Fez
• Type: private tour – your group only, with your own driver
• Guide: local guide at Volubilis included; your driver shows you around Meknes (a licensed city guide can be added)
• Driving: about 200 km in total, never more than 1 hour 15 minutes at a time
• Activity level: easy; about 3 to 4 km of walking during the day
• Best months: all year; from June to August we start early so Volubilis is visited before the heat

THE ROUTE
• Fez → Volubilis: about 85 km, 1 hour 15 minutes through the olive hills of the Saïss plain.
• Volubilis → Moulay Idriss: 5 km, 10 minutes.
• Moulay Idriss → Meknes: about 30 km, 40 minutes.
• Meknes → Fez: about 60 km, 1 hour on the motorway.

WHY THIS ORDER WORKS
Volubilis has almost no shade, so it is best early, when the light on the columns is soft and the site is quiet. Meknes, with its covered souks and shaded monuments, is comfortable in the afternoon. And because Meknes is only an hour from Fez on the motorway, you can stay until late afternoon and still be back for dinner.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Travellers spending three or more nights in Fez who want a change from the medina, history lovers, families with children who like ruins and big spaces, and anyone who wants to see a Moroccan imperial city without the crowds of Fez or Marrakech.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want more time in the holy town and less in Meknes, take the classic [Volubilis, Moulay Idriss and Meknes day trip](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/volubilis-moulay-idriss-meknes-day-trip-from-fes/bf42f86b52a477d92143db09), which walks through Moulay Idriss as well.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear comfortable shoes with a good grip: the paving stones of Volubilis are uneven and polished. Bring a hat, sun cream and water. Shoulders and knees covered is respectful in Moulay Idriss and at the mausoleum in Meknes. Entrance tickets are paid on site in dirhams, so carry cash; your driver tells you the current prices. Tell us your preferred pick-up time: 8:30 is usual, earlier in summer.
descriptions:
What to expect: a guided walk through the best-preserved Roman city in Morocco, a panorama over a holy town, and a relaxed afternoon in the imperial capital of Meknes.

Your driver collects you from your riad or hotel in Fez (if you stay inside the medina, at the nearest gate) and heads west across the Saïss plain, a landscape of olive groves, wheat fields and small farming villages, with the Zerhoun massif rising ahead.

VOLUBILIS (about 1.5 to 2 hours)
Volubilis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was one of the most remote cities of the Roman Empire, rich from olive oil and wheat. With your local guide you walk down the main street, the Decumanus Maximus, to the triumphal arch built in honour of Emperor Caracalla, see the columns of the basilica and the Capitol, and enter the houses of wealthy merchants where the floor mosaics are still in place: the Labours of Hercules, Orpheus charming the animals, the Bathing Nymphs. Storks often nest on top of the columns. Before you leave, look back from the upper part of the site for the classic view of the ruins with Moulay Idriss on the hill behind.

MOULAY IDRISS ZERHOUN (about 20–30 minutes)
A short drive brings you to the white town spread over two hills where Idris I, the founder of the first Moroccan dynasty, arrived in 789 and is buried. It is one of the most important pilgrimage places in the country. From a viewpoint above the town you see its houses tumbling around the green roofs of the shrine. Non-Muslims cannot enter the sanctuary itself, but the view gives you the whole story.

MEKNES (about 4 hours)
After lunch in the medina, you start at Place el-Hedim and the monumental gate of Bab Mansour, covered in green and white zellige tiles, often called the most beautiful gate in Morocco. Moulay Ismail, who ruled from 1672 to 1727, surrounded his capital with some 40 km of walls. Next come the granaries and stables of Heri es-Souani: huge vaulted halls, kept cool by thick walls and water channels, built to feed the city and thousands of horses during a siege, beside the large Agdal water basin. You then visit the Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail, one of the few royal tombs in Morocco that non-Muslim visitors may enter (when it is open), and end with free time in the medina and its souks, where the pace is slower than in Fez.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Pick-up in Fez.
09:45 – Volubilis: guided visit (1.5–2 hours).
11:45 – Moulay Idriss viewpoint (20–30 min).
12:30 – Arrival in Meknes; lunch in the medina (not included).
14:00 – Place el-Hedim and Bab Mansour.
14:45 – Heri es-Souani granaries and stables, Agdal basin.
15:45 – Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail.
16:30 – Free time in the medina and souks.
17:15 – Drive back to Fez (about 1 hour).
18:15 – Drop-off at your riad or hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Volubilis has very little shade: a hat and water are essential from April to October.
• Some monuments in Meknes close for restoration from time to time; your driver adapts the order of the visits.
• Dress modestly for Moulay Idriss and the mausoleum: shoulders and knees covered.
• Bring cash in dirhams for entrance tickets, lunch and small purchases.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, pick-up and drop-off in Fez, local guide at Volubilis, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance tickets, lunch, drinks, licensed city guide in Meknes (optional), tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Meknes is known for its olives: the stalls around Place el-Hedim sell dozens of kinds. For lunch, try a kefta tagine with egg, or a plate of grilled meat in a small restaurant near the square.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The Caracalla arch and the columns of the basilica at Volubilis, ideally in the morning light.
• Moulay Idriss from the viewpoint above the town.
• Bab Mansour from the far side of Place el-Hedim.
• The long rows of arches inside Heri es-Souani.

ACCESSIBILITY
Volubilis has uneven stone paths and gentle slopes; most of the main monuments can be seen without climbing. The main sites in Meknes are on flat ground. Tell us about any mobility needs and we will plan shorter walks.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: Rome and a Moroccan sultan's capital in a single day – and a quieter side of imperial Morocco.

faq.question: How far are Volubilis and Meknes from Fez?
faq.answer: Volubilis is about 85 km from Fez, around 1 hour 15 minutes by road. Meknes is about 30 km from Volubilis and 60 km from Fez, about one hour back on the motorway. The whole loop is around 200 km, split into short drives.

faq.question: How long do we spend at each place?
faq.answer: About 1.5 to 2 hours at Volubilis, 20 to 30 minutes at the Moulay Idriss viewpoint and around 4 hours in Meknes, including lunch. The day lasts about 9 hours from pick-up to drop-off, and you can stay longer anywhere you like.

faq.question: Is this a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Only your group travels in the vehicle, with your own driver. You choose the pick-up time and can change the pace or skip a stop on the day.

faq.question: Is a guide included?
faq.answer: A local guide is included at Volubilis, where explanations make the biggest difference. In Meknes your driver takes you to each site and gives you the background; if you want a licensed city guide for the medina and the monuments, we can arrange one for an extra fee.

faq.question: Are entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: No. Tickets for Volubilis and the monuments in Meknes are paid on site in dirhams. Prices are modest and change from time to time, so your driver will tell you the current amounts. Bring cash, as cards are not always accepted.

faq.question: Can we go inside the shrine at Moulay Idriss?
faq.answer: The sanctuary of Moulay Idriss is open to Muslims only. Non-Muslim visitors can see the town and its shrine from the viewpoint above and walk in the streets around it. The Mausoleum of Moulay Ismail in Meknes, by contrast, can be visited by non-Muslims when it is open.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with a good grip for the uneven stones of Volubilis, light clothing, a hat and sunglasses. For Moulay Idriss and the mausoleum, shoulders and knees should be covered; a light scarf is useful for women.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No, so you can choose what and where to eat. Your driver can recommend a restaurant in the Meknes medina or near Place el-Hedim, from simple grills to a sit-down meal with tagines.

faq.question: Is this trip suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children usually enjoy exploring the ruins, spotting storks on the columns and the huge halls of Heri es-Souani. Drives are short. Tell us their ages if you need child seats.

faq.question: Is it too hot in summer?
faq.answer: From June to August it can be very hot at Volubilis around midday. That is why we visit it first; in summer we suggest a pick-up around 7:30 so you are on the site before the heat. Bring water and a hat in any season.

faq.question: Can you pick us up inside the Fez medina?
faq.answer: Cars cannot enter the medina, so your driver meets you at the closest gate or parking to your riad. Many riads send someone to walk you there; tell us the name of your riad and we will arrange the exact meeting point.

faq.question: Can we end the tour in Meknes or continue to another city?
faq.answer: Yes. We can drop you at a hotel in Meknes or at the train station instead of returning to Fez. It is also possible to continue to Rabat or Chefchaouen as a longer transfer; ask us and we will plan the timing.

faq.question: What is the difference with your Volubilis, Moulay Idriss and Meknes day trip?
faq.answer: This tour gives most of the afternoon to Meknes and sees Moulay Idriss from the viewpoint. The [Volubilis, Moulay Idriss and Meknes day trip](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/volubilis-moulay-idriss-meknes-day-trip-from-fes/bf42f86b52a477d92143db09) includes a walk through Moulay Idriss and a shorter visit to Meknes. Choose this one if the imperial city interests you most.
